A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeXL study. The methods, equations, tables, figures and appendices are sufficiently readable and complete to match content across reformatting, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, ablations and case studies, plus Finance regression results in Appendix F, Tables 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification and regression experiments and adds encoder ablations, alternative-LLM evaluations and regression diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces v1's improvement-dependent stopping condition with an iteration cap, i < tau. It also explicitly saves validation-selected encoder/reflection checkpoints, although best-validation selection was already described in v1's prose. The encoder architecture, losses, fusion, prompts and regression adaptation are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Weather, Finance, Healthcare Test-Positive and Healthcare Mortality with the same classification tasks. Finance regression already appears in v1 Appendix F. The added analyses introduce no new dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds TimeMixer and FSCA to classification Table 1, and adds these methods plus TimeCAP to the regression comparison in Table 6, corresponding to v1 Table 5. PromptCast is removed from the corresponding component-ablation tables but remains in the benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: The new base-LLM comparison specifies matched prompts, iteration counts and other settings. Appendix F introduces prototype/input correlation assessment, while its regression ablations drop trend F1/AUC and retain RMSE, MAE and MAPE. The existing dataset splits and prediction horizons remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic analyses: single-modality encoder controls test modality contributions; Table 5 and Figure 8 test dependence on the base LLM; Appendix F adds regression iteration analysis and a case study with prototype/input correlations. The original learning-objective and prototype-count analyses remain, rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2 newly state that results average five experimental runs. v1 gives no corresponding run count. This is new reporting, not evidence that the number of runs increased; neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New comparator, modality-ablation, base-LLM and regression-diagnostic results substantially expand the empirical record. Existing TimeXL classification scores are unchanged, but LLMTime's Finance F1/AUC changes from 0.315/0.498 to 0.519/0.643. TimeXL regression RMSE/MAE/MAPE changes from 4.224/2.883/2.069 to 4.161/2.844/2.035; v2 Table 8 associates these with iterations 1 and 2, respectively, so this is not established as a fixed-iteration gain. Regression ablation values also change and their trend-score entries are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of representations, prototype similarities, regularizers, projection and prediction fusion are retained. Equations are combined or renumbered without substantive mathematical revision. No new assumptions, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: explainable prediction through prototype-encoder/LLM collaboration, evaluation on four datasets, and up to 8.9% AUC improvement. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly identifies long-horizon and domain-shift regression as unexplored extensions. Appendix B interprets the retained prototype-count experiment as an indirect explanation-quality measure and discusses LLM-as-judge evaluation without performing it. New passages also interpret base-LLM differences and the regression case study.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies Adam, the evaluated TimeCAP configuration, FSCA implementation and patch-size information, and generation settings for GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.0-Flash. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to previously undisclosed settings. Existing hardware and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix G substantially expand research positioning around multimodal fusion/alignment, alternative modality representations and LLM-based temporal reasoning. Added references include ReAct, Reflexion, Self-Refine and recent reasoning benchmarks, with explicit discussion distinguishing TimeXL's grounded, reflective model–LLM interaction.

P1.justification: Most core exposition is retained. Localized rewrites clarify optimization, experimental setup and ablations; related work gains a detailed appendix; the impact statement moves to Appendix I. Author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Prototype and workflow figures are rearranged or relabeled, ablation-table structures change, and new displays include base-LLM results, Finance prototypes/reflections, regression trajectories and correlation analysis.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports component attribution and model dependence through single-modality controls, alternative-LLM tests and expanded regression diagnostics. Clearer validation procedures, five-run reporting and specific limitations also improve assessability. These are bounded gains: explanation-quality evidence remains indirect, and dropping regression-ablation trend metrics removes useful information.
